lesson: Today, we work on one technique, the second person. That means the poem uses you and your to speak straight at the listener, as if you are the one doing the work. Here is where it does this. The wheelbarrow's grip has worn to your grain now. You take them up before your back has finished waking. Your breath goes out ahead of you. This works in a plain way. When you hear your back and your breath, your mind puts your own body in the scene. You are not watching a man push a wheelbarrow. You are pushing it. That is what holds your attention. Try this, write down one small morning chore, then put you and your in front of every part of the body and every object and read it back. The second time through, follow the word you and hear how sew up gives you the order.
